definitions.explanation: A wind blowing in the same direction one is traveling, making progress easier. Originally a nautical and aviation term.
Figuratively, circumstances that support progress or success. Often used in the expression {順風満帆|じゅんぷうまんぱん}.

examples.japanese: {順風|じゅんぷう}を{受|う}けて{船|ふね}が{進|すす}む。
examples.english: The ship moves forward with a tailwind.

examples.japanese: {飛行機|ひこうき}は{順風|じゅんぷう}のおかげで{予定|よてい}より{早|はや}く{到着|とうちゃく}した。
examples.english: The plane arrived earlier than scheduled thanks to a tailwind.

examples.japanese: {強|つよ}い{順風|じゅんぷう}に{乗|の}って{帆船|はんせん}はぐんぐん{進|すす}んだ。
examples.english: Riding a strong tailwind, the sailing ship surged forward.

examples.japanese: {事業|じぎょう}は{順風|じゅんぷう}に{乗|の}っている。
examples.english: The business is sailing with the wind.

examples.japanese: {彼|かれ}のキャリアは{順風満帆|じゅんぷうまんぱん}だ。
{順風|じゅんぷう}の{時|とき}こそ{油断|ゆだん}してはいけない。
examples.english: You must not let your guard down precisely when things are going well.

notes:
Composed of {順|じゅん} (favorable, following) and {風|ぷう} (wind). The figurative sense (smooth sailing) is more common in everyday usage than the literal nautical meaning.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {順風満帆|じゅんぷうまんぱん} — smooth sailing (literally 'favorable wind, full sails'); a very common four-character idiom
- {順風|じゅんぷう}に{乗|の}る — to ride a favorable wind; to have things going well

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {追|お}い{風|かぜ}: tailwind — more commonly used for the literal wind meaning in modern Japanese
- {向|む}かい{風|かぜ}: headwind — the opposite, both literally and figuratively
- {逆風|ぎゃくふう}: adverse wind, headwind — the formal antonym of {順風|じゅんぷう}
